description: OPS-ONLY. Cancel a run. Pass id to remove a not-yet-claimed queued job (a real cancel, no spend). Pass runId to file a cancel request on a started run. By default the cancel is COOPERATIVE — the sentinel is written and a turn already in flight is allowed to finish, which has no deadline: a reasoning turn can run for tens of minutes. Add immediate:true to also end that turn: it is sent a stop, anything of it still running a few seconds later is killed, and the answer says the turn ended only once it has seen it end. If it could not be ended, the run ends at its next step boundary, and the answer says that instead.

id.description: A queued job id (from start_run) — dequeues before the runner claims it.

immediate.description: Stop NOW instead of at the next step boundary. The cancel sentinel is written FIRST and then the run's own recorded engine turn is stopped, in that order — the sentinel is what makes the record clean, so the terminal names the stage, the actor and the request time instead of leaving a run that reads as still running. The turn is sent SIGTERM (to its whole process group when it leads one, as both engines spawn it, so the tools it started are reached too), watched, and sent SIGKILL if anything of it is still running when the grace runs out; the answer waits for that, which takes seconds. A turn that is stopped loses its step's work; everything already recorded is kept. Sending the stop is not the same as the turn ending, and the answer claims the second only when it has seen it (immediate.ended). Falls back to the boundary stop, and SAYS SO in the answer, when there is no live turn to signal — a run between steps, or one whose turn has already exited — or when the turn was still there after the SIGKILL. The answer states which of the two actually happened.

onBehalfOf.description: The identifier of a human this caller has itself verified. RECORDED BESIDE the token's own principal, never instead of it — a stop by the portal for alice@x is written `portal:alice@x`, so an asserted name is never mistaken for a proved one. Bare identifiers only; anything else is dropped.

runId.description: A started run's runId — files a cancel sentinel.

name: stop_run
